scenes.headline: How Blender 5.3 renders Gaussian splats
scenes.sub: Import, then three engines, and none of them sorts
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Fuzzy! Here's how Blender renders Gaussian splats, and why depth of field just works.

scenes.text: A splat becomes a typed point, and Cycles accepts each splat a ray meets by chance, so a splat is something a camera ray can hit.
scenes.mark: accepts each splat a ray meets by chance
scenes.say: The idea: a splat is a point, and Cycles lets a ray hit it, by chance.

scenes.title: From a scan file to a render

steps.say: A splat file stores raw training values: log scales and an opacity logit.
The importer exponentiates, squashes and normalizes them.
Out comes a point cloud with a type switch and named attributes.
The viewport dithers, the real-time engine hashes alpha, and Cycles traces rays.

scenes.title: One ray, one splat, in Cycles
scenes.say: A Gaussian has no surface. So how does a ray hit one?

items.say: Each splat gets a bounding sphere, sized from its opacity.

items.text: Find the peak along the ray
items.say: In the splat's own frame, its densest point is one dot product.
Hash that point. Below the Gaussian's response, the hit counts.
The nearest accepted hit wins, which averages to front to back blending.

left.title: The usual splat renderer
left.say: Usual renderers sort ellipses on screen and blend them.

right.title: Blender 5.3
right.say: Blender's accepted hits are opaque and have depth, so lenses work as on meshes.

scenes.title: Why the scan looks like a miniature
scenes.say: With an orthographic camera, the blur is simple.

parts.say: and with distance from focus, while nothing shrinks. That reads as a tiny model.

steps.say: Here's the bicycle scene, path traced in Cycles.
Every spoke is soft splats, each hit or passed by every ray.

scenes.title: Faint splats each engine skips
scenes.say: Faint splats differ: the real-time engine drops one in ten, Cycles one in six.

scenes.text: Turning transparency into chance gives every splat a real hit, so the whole renderer applies.

recap: Splats are typed points with attributes
Cycles accepts each hit by chance
Real hits, so depth of field works
scenes.say: To recap: splats are typed points, Cycles hits them by chance, and the lens just works.
